sources.title: Säten och huvudstöd
sources.locator: Whiplash protection and Minska riskerna; complete body retrieved via ?accessibilityarea=easyread
sources.excerpt: Är huvudstödet rätt utformat och inställt bör skaderisken kunna minska.
sources.supports: Head restraint/seat design and adjustment reduce rear-impact neck-injury risk; top at crown and small head gap.
sources.scope_limits: Explains protective purpose; no guarantee or claim that every whiplash mechanism is settled.

sources.title: Barn i bil
sources.locator: Opening explanation: relatively heavy head, undeveloped neck; rear-facing seat slows head and body together
sources.excerpt: en synkroniserad uppbromsning av huvud och kropp, varvid nacken skyddas
sources.supports: Rear-facing support slows head and body together and protects vulnerable neck.
sources.scope_limits: General safety/technical explanation; no foreign legal requirements imported.

sources.title: Så skyddar du barnen – regler och tips
sources.locator: Små barn åker säkrast bakåtvänt: heavy head, fragile neck and seat taking collision forces
sources.excerpt: En bakåtvänd stol tar emot de våldsamma krafterna
sources.supports: Seat supports head/neck and takes collision forces; combined with Trafikverket supports body-force distribution explanation.
sources.scope_limits: General safety/technical explanation; no foreign legal requirements imported.

sources.title: TSFS 2013:63 – vehicle technical requirements
sources.locator: Chapter 12 §§26 and 30; printed pp. 65–66 / PDF pp. 79–80
sources.excerpt: Färdbromsens transmission ska vara indelad i två eller flera kretsar.
sources.supports: Separate circuits and remaining, reduced braking capability after failure of one circuit.
sources.scope_limits: Technical purpose only. Regulation applicability depends on vehicle approval/date; no universal performance percentage or identical braking promise.

sources.title: TSFS 2017:54 – control inspection
sources.locator: Annex 1 §4.2.2 printed p.46 / PDF p.50; leakage/failure assessment §4.3 pp.50–51
sources.supports: A sinking pedal can indicate internal leakage; servo/pump behaviour can resemble it, so professional assessment is needed.
sources.scope_limits: Symptom suggests a possible fault, not a home diagnosis. Inspection test procedures and grading are not taught.

sources.publisher: Department for Infrastructure / Driver & Vehicle Agency, Northern Ireland government
sources.title: Taxi Driver Manual
sources.locator: Wheel balance p.47; hydraulic brakes p.49; Appendix 3 Basic vehicle faults p.181 (printed/PDF numbers agree)
sources.excerpt: Vibration in steering … Front wheel out of balance; brake pedal feels spongy … air in the brake system
sources.supports: Wheel imbalance is a possible vibration cause; air is a possible spongy hydraulic pedal cause.
sources.fallback_reason: Exact car-wheel imbalance and air/sponginess passages not located in targeted TS/TRV searches and current TS inspection text.
sources.scope_limits: Universal vehicle principles only, not Northern Ireland taxi rules. Several faults can cause similar symptoms.

sources.title: V60 Twin Engine – Reservhjul
sources.version: V60 Twin Engine model-year 2019 / 18w46; updated 19 March 2020
sources.locator: Temporary Spare use, Varning speed restriction and prescribed pressure; full indexed source passage retrieved; direct open failed
sources.supports: Temporary use, model-specific maximum speed and prescribed pressure. No numeric distance in this passage.
sources.fallback_reason: TS/TRV searches located no precise operating limits. Actual vehicle handbook is necessary; manufacturer is primary source for those limits.
sources.scope_limits: Illustrative 2019 Volvo handbook only. Its 80 km/h limit is not imported as a universal rule; check any stated distance/use restriction in actual handbook.

sources.title: The Highway Code – Rule 120
sources.excerpt: apply the footbrake firmly; do not release the pressure
sources.supports: Maintain firm pressure in emergency ABS braking; steering can remain possible; stopping distance not necessarily shorter.
sources.fallback_reason: Exact emergency pedal-action instruction not located in inspected TS/TRV pages.
sources.scope_limits: Common ABS operation only; no UK traffic law imported.

sources.title: 2011 Explorer Owner’s Guide
sources.locator: Four-wheel ABS / Using ABS, printed and PDF p.272 (zero-based index 271)
sources.excerpt: brake pedal pulsation may be observed during ABS braking
sources.supports: Normal ABS pulsation and continuous pressure rather than pumping.
sources.fallback_reason: Official Rule 120 supplies the driver action but not pulsation. Exact TS/TRV normal-feedback explanation not located; manufacturer passage verifies the technical feedback.
sources.scope_limits: Model-qualified evidence of ABS feedback. No claim that every vibration is ABS or that ABS always shortens a stop.

sources.supports: Controlled front/rear deformation absorbs crash energy while structure protects passenger compartment; reduced deceleration/forces.
sources.fallback_reason: Targeted TS/TRV searches did not yield the exact deformation/energy mechanism.
sources.scope_limits: Shared engineering principle only; no foreign ratings or buying rules imported.
